The decay rate is related to half life by . A sample having N0 radioactive nuclei at time t = 0 will have radioactive nuclei at time t. Thus, activity (A = N) of a sample reduces from its initial value A0 to a value at time t.

Let V be the total volume of blood and N be the total number of radioactive nuclei at time t. The nuclei are distributed uniformly in blood. A sample of volume v will have n = (v/V)N radioactive nuclei in it. Thus, activity of this sample is

.

Substitute a = 115 Bq, v = 2.5 ml, A0 = 2.4 105 Bq, = ln 2/t1/2 0.7/(8 24) hr1 and t = 11.5 hr to get

= 4998 ml 5 litre.
